title: Figaro Delivery Lifecycle Schema v1
description: Off-chain schema definition for the figaro-delivery-lifecycle-v1 attestation schema. Defines the delivery lifecycle stages, their stage encodings, role assignments, and contentRef formats for Figaro local-commerce and logistics process graphs (food delivery, retail courier, parcel courier, etc.).

0.name: PreparationStarted
0.description: The seller (merchant — restaurant, retailer, service-provider, or logistics handler) has begun preparing the order. Attested by the seller of the root order node. Signals that the order is in active fulfilment and courier dispatch can begin.
0.contentRefFormat: bytes32(0) — no content payload required. Stage is a pure lifecycle signal.

1.name: ReadyForPickup
1.description: The seller has completed preparation and the order is ready for collection by the courier. Attested by the seller. Triggers courier dispatch and Dutch auction entry if not yet claimed.
1.contentRefFormat: bytes32(0) — no content payload required. Optionally: keccak256 of a location geohash string for pickup point.

2.name: CourierEnRoute
2.description: The courier (driver, cyclist, walker, drone, autonomous vehicle, etc.) has accepted the job and is en route to the pickup location. Attested by the seller of the delivery sub-order (the courier). Requires a valid delivery sub-order in the same process.
2.contentRefFormat: bytes32(0) — no content payload required. Optionally: keccak256 of a proximity proof JSON string (see figaro-proximity-proof-v1).

3.name: PickedUp
3.description: The courier has collected the order from the seller. Attested by the seller of the delivery sub-order (the courier) via cross-order attestation on the root order hash. Optionally includes a proximity proof.
3.contentRefFormat: bytes32(0) for no proof, or encodeProximityProofRef(proof) — keccak256 of proximity proof JSON. See figaro-proximity-proof-v1 for proof encoding.

4.name: Delivered
4.description: The courier has delivered the order to the buyer. Final delivery signal. Attested by the courier via cross-order attestation on the root order hash. Optionally includes a proximity proof for the handoff.
4.contentRefFormat: bytes32(0) for no proof, or encodeProximityProofRef(proof) — keccak256 of proximity proof JSON. See figaro-proximity-proof-v1.

roleAssignment.description: Stage attestation is role-gated by AttestationCoordinator. Callers prove role by supplying their commitment struct. The coordinator recomputes the orderHash and extracts seller/buyer from on-chain state.
roleAssignment.seller: Stages 0 and 1. The seller of the root order (merchant — restaurant, retailer, service-provider, or primary handler) attests preparation and readiness. Must call attestAsSeller with the root order commitment.
roleAssignment.courier: Stages 2, 3, and 4. The seller of the delivery sub-order attests delivery progress. Must call attestAsSeller with the delivery sub-order commitment (cross-order attestation on the root orderHash).
roleAssignment.buyer: No mandatory lifecycle stage. May optionally attest receipt confirmation under a separate schema (e.g. figaro-commerce-v1 stage 5).

processTreeBinding.description: Lifecycle attestations attach to a specific orderHash within a processId. The root order represents the primary transaction (buyer ↔ merchant). Delivery sub-orders are child orders (buyer ↔ courier) within the same process.
processTreeBinding.rootOrderRole: PreparationStarted (0) and ReadyForPickup (1) attest on the root orderHash by the root seller.
processTreeBinding.subOrderRole: CourierEnRoute (2), PickedUp (3), and Delivered (4) attest on the root orderHash by the courier, proving role via the delivery sub-order commitment.
processTreeBinding.crossOrderAttestation: Couriers must supply the delivery sub-order commitment to attestAsSeller, with the root orderHash as the target. The coordinator verifies both orders belong to the same processId.

indexingNotes.description: Indexers reconstructing delivery status from events should process Attestation events in block order. For each (processId, orderHash) pair, the highest stage seen is the current status.
indexingNotes.stageOrdering: Stages are not strictly sequential on-chain — an indexer should track the set of emitted stages rather than assuming a monotonic progression.
indexingNotes.courierIdentification: The courier address is the attester of stages 2–4. Cross-reference with the delivery sub-order seller address for identity verification.
